 Park Jin Young had a career-defining role in '100 Days of Lies'.
 After years of being known as a member of GOT7, Park Jin Young is making significant strides in his acting career thanks to his role as Kim Tae Woong in 100 Days of Lies.
 Báo Tuổi Trẻ • 10/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Park Jin Young's popularity soared after the success of "100 Days of Lies" - Photo: tvN
 According to Ten Asia , 100 Days of Deception is currently one of the most talked-about dramas on Korean television. It has held the number one spot in TV drama popularity for three consecutive weeks, achieving a rating of 10.7% in episode 10.
 In the FUNdex actor rankings released in early November, Park Jin Young topped the list with 3.84%, surpassing both Kim Yoo Jung and Kim Ji Won. This shows his increasing popularity after more than 10 years in the entertainment industry.
 Park Jin Young breaks the stereotype of idols acting in movies.
 Before gaining audience attention for his role in 100 Days of Deception , Park Jin Young had a rather long artistic journey.
 He started learning to dance when he was in middle school. Because there were no professional dance training centers in his hometown, Park Jin Young often traveled a long three-hour journey to Busan to attend classes. 
 Park Jin Young (far left) during his time with GOT7 - Photo: JYP Entertainment
 In 2009, he auditioned for JYP Entertainment along with Jay B. Both ranked first among over 10,000 contestants and became trainees at the company.
 In January 2012, Park Jin Young had his acting debut in the KBS drama Dream High 2. Four months later, he made his musical debut with Jay B in the group JJ Project.
 After a break of about 18 months, both returned in January 2014 as members of GOT7.
 Music has never been the only path Park Jin Young has pursued. During his time with GOT7, Jin Young regularly took on acting projects.
 In 2015, he gained attention for his role as the teenage male lead in JTBC's My Love Eun Dong .
 You may also like The actor's ability to express emotions received positive feedback, opening up more opportunities to try his hand at more profound roles. In 2017, he continued to take on the lead role in Magic School. 
 Park Jin Young in Yumi's Cells impressed viewers with his captivating appearance and the complexities of his emotions - Photo: tvN
 One of the roles that brought Park Jin Young closer to television viewers was Yoo Ba Bi in Yumi's Cells . The character , with her attractive appearance but complex romantic feelings, required him to portray many psychological nuances.
 However, perhaps the biggest turning point was when he took on the roles of twin brothers in the thriller Christmas Carol . One has a developmental disability, while the other carries the pain and determination to avenge his brother's death.
 The role earned him the Best New Actor award at the 59th Baeksang Arts Awards and the 43rd Korean Film Critics Association Awards. 
 Park Jin Young breaks the stereotype of idols acting in films after Christmas Carol - Photo: IMDb
 Eyes speak louder than words in 100 Days of Deception. 
 In 100 Days of Deception , Park Jin Young plays Sato Hideo, an elite interpreter working for Japan in Korea. Behind that Japanese name is Kim Tae Woong, a Korean who was adopted by a Japanese military officer.
 Growing up between two cultures and two identities, the character is constantly confronted with conflicts about their origins, loyalty, and true place in the world. 
 Kim Tae Woong has feelings for Lee Ga Kyung but is torn between responsibility, love, and the guilt about his true identity - Photo: tvN
 Kim Tae Woong falls in love with the female thief Lee Ga Kyung (Kim Yoo Jung). His feelings for Ga Kyung cause him further conflict, as he also longs for the recognition of his adoptive father, Sato Shinichi, played by Jin Seon Kyu.
 You may also like A notable aspect of Park Jin Young's portrayal of Tae Woong is his restraint. The character rarely directly expresses his emotions, even when in front of the person he loves or facing deep-seated trauma.
 Before episode 7 aired, director Yoo In Sik gave special praise to Park Jin Young's eyes. He commented, "Park Jin Young has incredibly clear eyes. When I look into his eyes, I immediately feel the innocence in his gaze." 
 The director emphasized Jin Young's ability to subtly change his gaze when the character falls into a state of hesitation or pain - Photo: tvN
 Korean media also praised Park Jin Young's acting abilities. The Korea Herald was impressed by how Park Jin Young didn't need to constantly use strong expressions to convey Kim Tae Woong's inner conflict.
 Even subtle changes in his gaze are enough to create moments of silence, allowing the audience to understand what the character cannot express in words. This restraint also contributes to a performance that is different from the familiar romantic male lead roles Jin Young has previously played.
